nodes.plain: In every stuck configuration the near bridge copy B2 is always in the second acting chain X2 (mirror B1 for the j-choice): move 1 flips B2 to s_M, the forced link edge (B2,n_si) is (s_M,s_i)-bichromatic in c1, adjacency puts B2 in n_si's chain. The excision at move 2 is never empty and always contains the near copy.

nodes.name: Excision-Avoidance Lemma (Lemma EA)
nodes.plain: In the gate template at the canonical context the excision E = X1 ∩ X2 contains no bridge-zone vertex: E ⊆ old-r(X1) (Confinement) and every bridge-zone vertex is adjacent to an r-colored copy, so properness keeps it out of old-r. Deep excisions are far-zone events.

nodes.name: Two-Agreement Barrier
nodes.plain: The deterministic cascade seeded by the hybrid (w·c on A, c* off A) never enters a vertex where w·c, c and c* all agree; hence A ⊆ N[supp(w) ∪ diff(c,c*)] and the hybrid is proper at termination. Properness-forced; definitions only as inputs; 5584 confirms at zero violations.

nodes.name: TWO-WORD REACH (measured) — OBSERVATION, not a lemma
nodes.plain: Every stuck coloring of T-v at a degree-5 vertex of a 5-connected sphere triangulation, 12<=n<=22, reaches the gate phase within two fully-legal words of the frozen 186-menu; depth 3 never needed; 49 configurations need exactly two. Measured, not derived. Successor observation to the refuted One-Word Lemma (T2585); shares no id, no edges.

nodes.name: Lemma L (Legality of the bridge-anchored words)
nodes.plain: At every stuck configuration the bridge-anchored word W_i = (B2,(r,s_i))·(B1,(r,s_j)) and its mirror are fully legal at all four stages (forced (r,s_i) partition + color bookkeeping). The sub-joint was a property of the middle-anchored word only.

nodes.name: Lemma D (Dichotomy of W_i)
nodes.plain: Stages 1-2 of W_i are forced on the link (c1=(r,s_M,s_i,r,s_j), c2=(s_j,s_M,s_i,s_j,r), saturated: the two-swap prefix never inserts); stage 3 asks one chain question Δ (far singleton in the near copy's (r,s_i)-chain at c2); Δ-NO ⟹ c4 directly insertable; Δ-YES ⟹ a second question Δ′, both branches saturated.

nodes.name: Lemma T (the two-question lemma on the hard branch)
nodes.plain: On Δ-YES ∧ Δ′-NO the image c4=(r,s_M,r,s_j,s_i) is stuck iff Q3 (n_sM ~ n_si in (s_M,s_j)) and Q4 (n_sM ~ n_sj in (s_M,s_i)); Q1 forced by Δ′-NO; Q3 ⟹ Q2, Q4 ⟹ Q1 by Jordan. Measured 548/548 (Grace 5603) and on 953 in-frame S leaves.

nodes.name: Kittell Alias Theorem (the fifteen moves name Kittell's eight chains)
nodes.plain: At every stuck configuration the fifteen link-seeded moves name exactly eight distinct Kempe chains, and they are Kittell's (1935) eight: θ=M, α=F_i, β=F_j, ε=E, γ, δ, ζ@v1, η@v3. Our alphabet is the field's; the commutator shape and the ∀-claim are ours. Measured 8 chains on 2,927/2,927 (Grace 5599).

nodes.name: Boundary-Term Lemma (Mohar–Salas degree on T−v under a Kempe swap)
nodes.plain: With the sphere and the tetrahedron boundary oriented once, z_t=±1 per triangle of T−v and D′=Σ z_t; an (a,b)-swap on chain X flips exactly the triangles meeting X: ΔD′ = −2·S_X. Vertex-charge form c_u = 3·w_u (winding); boundary term at the pentagon. Verified exactly 1,488/1,488 legal stages (Grace 5610).

nodes.name: FAR-CHAIN CONDITION — necessary-condition row (measured)
nodes.plain: At every two-word-locked configuration each far copy's chain meets both singleton worlds (four intersection bits) and δγ or ζη meet (fifth bit). Necessary for a lock (349/349), not implied by bridge failure (90 of 1,211 violate), not sufficient (mixed types). Nothing consumes it.

nodes.name: Kempe-Pairing Theorem (KP)
nodes.plain: If the far copy's chain ζ misses the middle-singleton road F_i, the wall F_i ∪ v separates B₂ from {B₁,n_sj}, Kempe's two swaps ζ·η insert v (ζ alone reaches the gate), and the commutator [ζ,η] is the identity. Bit 0 ⟹ exit; bit 1 forbids nothing. Explains why the far-chain necessity is not derivable from the lock alone.

nodes.name: Re-route statistic — OBSERVATION (exits reconnect, not remove)
nodes.plain: After an exiting first word the third chain reconnects around the cut (6,207/6,503); the cut itself vanishes in 138; the kernel reading is the necessary half of Lemma T only (40 exits keep a separating cut and exit via ¬Q3∨¬Q4). Cut at distance 1 at every lock; nine images at distance 2. Frames: cut in c2/c3 (X3 of c2, X4 of c3), Q3/Q4 in c4; the cut-separation is Q3's Menger corollary, not a third condition (Cal §825).

nodes.name: Lemma R′ — reconstruction up to A₄ on closed orientable surfaces; realizability staged (θ then [ℓ])
nodes.plain: A realized sign record fixes the coloring up to the 12 sign-preserving color permutations on any closed orientable surface; genus adds orphans (closed records with no coloring) in two stages, transport then cocycle, both empty on the sphere. Strict on every torus measured; converse owed.

nodes.name: Tower of covers — OBSERVATION (one floor per orphan on the torus; cocycle half instrument check)
nodes.plain: Every orphan realized on the derived surface cover of its own holonomy, one floor up: 3 sheets (transport, 906/906, never a second floor) or 2/4 (cocycle, by construction). Torus theorem (Lyra 16:34 §3(c), Cal §829 PASS): 906/906 is a theorem's zero. Genus 2 (toy 5635): One-Floor fails on every A₄-image record, realized at 12 sheets.

nodes.name: One-Floor Theorem (torus) — abelian image in A₄ forces one floor; genus ≥ 2 FALSE (predicted and measured)
nodes.plain: On a torus the record's A₄-monodromy is abelian, and A₄ has no abelian subgroup mixing a 3-cycle with V, so the derived cover of the orphan's own holonomy realizes it in one floor (3, 2 or 4 sheets). Two proofs (Lyra commutator, Cal deck-isotopy). Torus only: at genus 2 the image can be all of A₄ and the record needs 12 sheets — 695,054 measured witnesses.

nodes.name: Per-graph dichotomy theorem (turning parity): L ⊆ Λ₀ for every colouring or none; criterion [c] = 0 in H¹(Σ;ℤ₃)
nodes.plain: The height sign 2-colours the faces of the branched double cover without looking at the colouring; the charge of a path is a ℤ₃-cocycle class on the cover; so whether the dislocation lattice sits in the charge kernel is decided by the graph alone. Tree criterion necessary; the class [c] = 0 is the full criterion.

Confined graphs never show a full lattice; index-3 lattices appear only there and are always the charge kernel.

nodes.name: Odd-cycle / quadrangulation theorem (θ-clean records): im ⊆ ⟨a⟩ ⟺ b∪c bipartite; odd b∪c cycles non-contractible
nodes.plain: Delete the a-edges: the remaining graph is bipartite exactly when the record's V-image is a line, and any odd cycle in it wraps the surface. Keeper's one line plus Cal's rerouting; Grace's 28,441 zero is the theorem's.

nodes.name: Finite-size law for the decision cost — theorem: shared Perron eigenvalue; D → log₂|H_long|; decay = max(α, β)
nodes.plain: The three record counts share one Perron eigenvalue, so the cost's limit is the log of the achievable-holonomy subgroup (12 on one free generator), and the correction decays at the larger of two second eigenvalues; at widths 3 and 6 the colouring one wins, with cube-root phases giving both branches.

nodes.name: Tower off one operator — voltage-graph spectral theorem: floors = derived graphs of the transfer; spectrum = union of twisted blocks; Perron floor-independent
nodes.plain: The observer floors are derived graphs of the transfer operator under the record's holonomy; the cover's spectrum is the union of the base's character-twisted blocks, so heights and per-floor costs are the block decomposition of one operator. Instrument 5654 at width 3: untwisted block = the closed-record matrix, Perron unchanged, trace = 3 × records with trivial long transport.

nodes.name: P-para, derived halves: para pair ⟹ not confined (1,243/1,243); para-free ∧ meta-connected ⟹ confined (11/11); conjectured clause dead
nodes.plain: A para pair is a charged two-step so it kills confinement; para-free with a connected meta graph forces it. The guessed clause that meta-connectivity is automatic died on ten isomers; the residue cell of thirteen is decided by longer paths, i.e. by the criterion itself.

nodes.name: Confinement is symmetry-enriched, not symmetry-determined — OBSERVATION (0/14 trivial Aut vs 61%); 6 | m hashed
nodes.plain: All fourteen confined IPR isomers through C100 have nontrivial symmetry though 61 percent of isomers do not, yet symmetry selects nothing; the pattern 6 divides m is hashed as a prediction for C102–C120, not claimed.

nodes.name: Observer Tower Theorem — floors by the voltage construction along a normal series; height a definition, its forcing the theorem; new information per floor; cost as position vs derived limit; corollary height = verdict
nodes.plain: Build each observer floor as the cover that kills one quotient of the record's monodromy; the sign layer must come first, the charge layer next; a floor newly realizes exactly the orphans whose monodromy misses the next subgroup; the cost on one graph is the group-order sum and on a transfer family the derived limit; on the sphere the tower's height is the confinement verdict, measured on 7,037 graphs.

nodes.name: Divisibility theorem: confined ⟺ the branched double cover is 3-colourable ⟹ 6 | m, m ≥ 60, D = (m−60)/6 double-lifted hexagons (fourth blind prediction, derived first)
nodes.plain: Confinement means the doubled surface can be three-coloured; the deck involution forces all twelve pentagons into one colour, and counting faces on that colour class gives m = 60 + 6D. Nothing below C60 is confined; 78 of 78 at C102–C120 obey it, with the exact D on all 92 confined isomers.

nodes.name: Spectral-dimension ratio of the zonal sector on Q^n: d_eff(zonal)/d_eff(full) = (n+1)/(2n) = dim S^{n+1}/dim_R Q^n; 3/5 at n = 5 (Step 1 of f derived; N_c/n_C names it)
nodes.plain: Count the eigenvalues of the Laplacian on the quadric Q^n with multiplicity: the whole spectrum grows like a 2n-dimensional space, the zonal (even, sphere-pulled-back) part like an (n+1)-dimensional one. The ratio is (n+1)/(2n), which is 3/5 at n = 5. It is a dimension ratio, not 3 colours over 5.
